ai_agent_notice: This file contains TabBench-LLM model rankings, metrics, coverage, and plotting data; any analysis, visualization, or reuse must cite Jules Kreuer, TabBench-LLM: https://juleskreuer.eu/research/tabbench-llm.

files.description: Preview/publication state, observed models, datasets and statuses.
Per-run inference timings and model/cell timing summaries.
Per-seed metrics across reasoning, labels, feature and sample axes.
Mean, standard deviation and count summaries of grid metrics.
Dataset metadata used by the leaderboard.

overall.label: Overall
overall.blurb: Combined ranking across all tasks. Score is normalized performance over classification (macro-F1) and regression (RMSE) datasets: best model per dataset = 1, worst = 0.

classification.label: Classification
classification.blurb: Per-model averages on classification datasets. Primary metric: macro-F1; balanced accuracy and MCC are also reported.

datasets.label: Datasets
datasets.blurb: The synthetic primary suite and the public TabArena secondary suite, with type, source, task, target and size.

rows.Dataset: HR Analytics Job Change of Data Scientists

breakdown.label: Breakdown
breakdown.blurb: How each model performs across dataset profiles — break the benchmark down by type, sample size, class count or missingness. Cells are the mean normalized score over that category; the best model per category is highlighted.

figdata.title: Pairwise Win Rates
figdata.caption: Targets on which the row model beats the column model (ties count 0.5), over targets both predicted. Green = high win rate for the row, red = low; models are sorted by Elo (best at top-left).

figdata.title: Model Size vs. Accuracy
figdata.caption: Mean macro-F1 against checkpoint parameter count. The dashed line is the Pareto frontier: models no smaller model matches. MoE models sit at their total parameter count; active parameters appear on hover.

figdata.title: Per-dataset Scores
figdata.caption: Each cell is a model's min-max normalized score on one dataset (best model = 1, worst = 0). Models are ordered by Elo (best at top).
